Your agent runs 40 seconds across six tool calls. A mid-run deploy restart means you pay for every tool call twice.

8 min read
Just now

--

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Senior engineers will want to know how to prevent deploy-induced agent restarts and avoid redundant tool calls in their Rails apps.Your agent runs 40 seconds across six tool calls. Someone ships a deploy at second 31.
Kamal gives a job-running container 30 seconds to shut down by default before it kills it. Your agent was still inside tool call five.
That is not an edge case in a durable AI agent workflow. Every deploy is a chance for this to happen, and every time it does, you pay for the four tool calls that already ran and then pay again to run all six from scratch.
Rails 8.1 shipped ActiveJob::Continuable specifically to stop jobs from restarting at zero. It does not automatically make an agent loop resumable, and the gap between Continuable exists and your agent survives a deploy is where most of this article's usefulness lives.
Job starts
↓
step :call_tool_1 → checkpoint
↓
step :call_tool_2 → checkpoint
↓
...deploy hits here, job pauses...
↓
Job resumes → step :call_tool_4 (steps 1-3 skipped, already checkpointed)
• Checkpoint once per tool call inside a single ActiveJob::Continuable step, using step.advance! as each tool call finishes…
